summary.one_liner: A Claude Code plugin that turns an Obsidian vault into a structured, entity-typed Zettelkasten knowledge graph managed by AI skills.
keywords: keep notes in sync with sources
summary.what_it_does: Bedrock is a Claude Code plugin that manages an Obsidian vault through eight skills: setup, ask, learn, preserve, compress, sync, healthcheck, and vaults. Notes are organized into seven entity types (actors, people, teams, topics, discussions, projects, and fleeting notes), each with a _template.md defining its frontmatter. The README says that /bedrock:learn and /bedrock:sync ingest Confluence, Google Docs, GitHub repositories, and any file docling supports (such as DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, PDF, HTML, EPUB, and images), then create entities with bidirectional wikilinks. Entities get hierarchical tags like type/, status/, domain/, and scope/. /bedrock:ask answers questions by searching the graph and vault with citations, and /bedrock:compress and /bedrock:healthcheck handle broken links, orphans, and duplicates. Configuration lives in .bedrock/config.json inside the vault.
use_cases: Turn a folder of documents into a linked Obsidian knowledge base
Import Confluence pages or Google Docs into a vault as notes
Ask questions about systems, owners, and project status across notes
Keep vault notes updated from external sources
Find and fix broken wikilinks, orphan notes, and duplicate entries
Organize team knowledge with people, teams, and projects entities
stack: Python (implied by tracebacks and pipx install)
notable: Entity-typed Zettelkasten structure with permanent, bridge, index, and fleeting note roles
Ingests Confluence and Google Docs through built-in internal skills, with no separate install
Opt-out error reporting that files GitHub issues but excludes vault content, absolute paths, and entity names
Multi-vault support with a --vault flag and a vaults management skill
Setup wizard offers presets such as engineering team, product management, and personal second brain
caveats: graphify is required, and docling is required; both are auto-installed by setup or learn on first use
Error reporting is on by default and needs an authenticated gh CLI; without it, reports are only logged locally
The README does not describe platform support beyond Claude Code and Obsidian
